summary.text: The exponential distribution has a rate parameter λ > 0, takes values on the interval [0, ∞), and is used to analyze Poisson point processes among other contexts.
A person who receives an average of two phone calls per hour can expect about 0.5 hours, or 30 minutes, between consecutive calls.
It is memoryless: after a wait with no event, the remaining wait has the same distribution as at the start, and it is the only continuous distribution with a constant failure rate.

facts.label: Memoryless pair
facts.value: Only the exponential and geometric distributions are memoryless

facts.label: Failure rate
facts.value: The only continuous distribution with a constant failure rate

facts.label: Sums
facts.value: The sum of n independent Exp(λ) variables is Gamma(n, λ)

items.prompt: A person gets an average of two phone calls per hour. What is the typical time between consecutive calls?

options.label: 2 hours
1 hour
15 minutes
30 minutes

items.explain: With an average of two calls per hour, the expected time between consecutive calls is 0.5 hour, or 30 minutes.

items.prompt: An event has not happened after 30 seconds of waiting. The waiting time is exponential. How does the chance of at least 10 more seconds compare with the chance of waiting over 10 seconds from the start?

options.label: It is equal
It is smaller, because the event is now due
It is larger, because the event keeps delaying
It cannot be compared at all

items.explain: The conditional probability of waiting at least 10 more seconds equals the unconditional probability of more than 10 seconds.

items.prompt: A shopper has waited a long time for an event with an exponential waiting time and says it must be due. What is wrong with that?

options.label: Long waits make the event even less likely
The remaining wait has the same distribution as when she began
The event only happens right at the start
Waiting times cannot be measured once started

items.explain: Given no event over an initial period, the distribution of the remaining wait is the same as the original distribution.

items.prompt: Waiting times can never be negative. Which range of values does the exponential distribution use?

options.label: All real numbers, positive and negative
Only the numbers between 0 and 1
From 0 upward, with no upper limit
Only the whole numbers 1, 2, 3 and so on

items.explain: The distribution is supported on the interval [0, ∞).

items.prompt: A machine part is equally likely to fail in any next moment, however long it has already run. Which continuous distribution matches this constant failure rate?

options.label: A normal distribution
A uniform distribution
A Poisson distribution
An exponential distribution

items.explain: The exponential distribution is the only continuous probability distribution with a constant failure rate.

items.prompt: A job needs three separate waits one after another, each independent and exponential with the same rate. What describes the total time?

options.label: A gamma distribution
Another exponential with the same rate
A normal distribution with mean zero
A fixed number with no spread

items.explain: The sum of n independent exponential variables with rate λ follows a Gamma(n, λ) distribution.
